The question's premise is reversed. The lower-manganese LNO sample, not the higher-manganese sample, delivered more capacity: 212 mAh g^− 1[1] against 164 mAh g^− 1[2]. Higher Mn content lowered capacity, which the paper attributes to the electrochemical inactivity of Mn4+ ions.

For heat release in the thermal decomposition tests, the lower-Mn sample released more heat, not less: 901.4 J g^−1[3], while the higher-Mn sample released 485.7 J g^−1[4].

So the higher-Mn sample released less heat, by this difference in J/g: 415.7[5] J/g less than the lower-Mn sample, as the paper's sentence on cathode systems with lower Mn content reports.
